title: 360 ONE WAM LTD - 542772 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: 360 ONE WAM Q2 FY27: revenue ₹853 crores (+4.8% YoY), PAT ₹302 crores, ARR AUM ₹3.53 lakh crores (+19.7% YoY), ARR net flows ₹12,482 crores.
summary.overview: Total AUM was about ₹9 lakh crores (+31% YoY) and ARR revenue grew 27.5% YoY to ₹706 crores, now 79% of operating revenue. Headline revenue growth was held back by a negative ₹44 crore other income from mark-to-market on treasury investments, mainly NSE-linked fair value change of about ₹110-120 crores. Carry from third-party funds contributed about ₹60 crores, lifting ARR retention to 79 bps from 74 bps in Q1 (67 bps ex-carry). Cost-to-operating income improved to 51.5% from 54.3% in Q1, and tangible ROE was 16.9%.

financial_highlights.change: +15.5% YoY; employee costs ₹342 crores (+19.9%) incl. ~₹9 crores one-time restructuring

segments.name: Wealth
segments.commentary: ARR AUM ₹2,52,627 crores (+24.3% YoY); net flows ₹10,990 crores; ARR revenue ₹503 crores (+40.5% YoY); retention 79 bps (71 bps in Q1); operating PBT ₹326 crores (+30.2% YoY).

segments.name: Asset management
segments.commentary: ARR AUM a little over ₹1 lakh crores (+9.4% YoY); net flows ₹1,492 crores after large SMA redemptions in Q1; ARR revenue ₹203 crores at 79 bps; operating PBT ₹108 crores.

segments.name: Alternates (AIF)
segments.commentary: AIF AUM ₹58,139 crores (+27.9% YoY). Q2 AIF distributions about ₹2,500 crores vs net inflows about ₹2,500 crores, implying gross inflows of ₹4,800-4,900 crores.

segments.name: HNI business
segments.commentary: Manages over ₹8,000 crores for over 1,500 clients with about 60 RMs; ~2,000 relationships moved from UHNI, taking HNI AUM to ~₹8,800 crores; expects break-even on direct costs soon.

guidance_outlook: Cost-to-operating income: guided 100-150 bps YoY improvement; management says on course, with a path toward 46-47% from 48% over 12-18 months.

UBS collaboration: internal target of about $600-650 million of flows exchanged in FY27; about $300-325 million moved in last three months; expects $600-700 million over the year. Expected retention on cross-flows 40-50 bps.
Tangible ROE: target around 20% over 3-3.5 years by doubling profits, with no equity raise needed; possible push toward 25% later. UBS warrant conversion (~₹1,600 crores) expected around February.
Capital markets: full-stack platform ready by end-March/early April 2027; banking and ECM mandates expected to flow from Q1 FY28; 8-10 issues appointed so far.
Equity brokerage from HNI/UHNI clients rose from ₹4.5-5 crores to ₹8-9 crores a month; potential ₹15-20 crores a month.
Fund P1A redemption of about ₹3,000-3,500 crores expected over the next 6-18 months.
capex_capacity: Tangible net worth about ₹7,400 crores, plus ~₹1,600 crores from UBS; management sees ~₹10,000-12,000 crores over the period with PAT of ~₹1,000-1,200 crores per year post dividend.
COMPASS proprietary AI layer is live across wealth, asset management and enterprise functions; runs inside the 360 ONE environment with no client data used to train external models.
ET Money ARR AUM about ₹3,300-3,400 crores including the distribution segment (over ₹700 crores ARR AUM in the last nine months).
demand_pricing: Q2 flows were supported by a strong IPO season (about 60 IPOs in the quarter) and monetization events; NSE listing was a major event. Wealth flows split about 50% from wallet share and 50% from new mandates, versus the usual 65-70% from new mandates.
New clients were about one-third of flows, existing clients two-thirds (management's broad split). Client attrition below 0.5% and AUM attrition below 0.25%.
Advisory retention on core portfolios 35-40 bps; large mandates around 20-25 bps; overall relationship retention 65-73 bps.
Management sees TBR as ~₹200-225 crores a quarter on ~₹1,000 crores revenue, growing late single to early double digits; mostly brokerage across six or seven asset classes.
On competition, management sees no dramatic margin compression; differentiation expected from people, product and platform together.
Mutual fund business: management plans measured growth, with possible sales-team build-out given SIF launch and 4-5 years of performance.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the mark-to-market change so large and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to secondaries market pricing; NSE-related fair value change of about ₹110-120 crores, largely held through funds. Prior quarter had a positive move.

qa_highlights.question: How do UBS flows progress and when do they come through?
qa_highlights.answer: About $300-325 million of flows moved in the last three months, with a target of $600-700 million for the year; funds recently empanelled and about $15 million came from UBS to 360 ONE initially.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company on track for the 48% cost-to-income target?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO says on course for 100-150 bps YoY improvement; management targets a move from 48% toward 46-47% over 12-18 months, with productivity gains mainly in employee costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the role of new leadership hire Ashish Agarwal and the cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Senior leadership role spearheading the business with Karan Bhagat; first 6-8 months focused on integration. Three hires so far; cost-to-income could rise 100-200 bps during a big build, but expected to stay within that band.

qa_highlights.question: Why was AMC flow weaker, and what about carry reversals?
qa_highlights.answer: One institutional redemption split between Q1 and Q2; two institutional mandates won late in the quarter. Carry reversal on previously accrued NSE-linked carry was more than offset by new carry from NSE listing bringing funds into carry.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TBR outlook and how big are broking synergies from B&K?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says TBR is now mainly brokerage and was soft; expects ~₹800-1,000 crores TBR at ₹5,000-5,500 crores revenue. Equity brokerage from HNI/UHNI rose from ₹4.5-5 crores to ₹8-9 crores a month.

qa_highlights.question: How should AMC gross outflows be thought of from carry-linked funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Fund P1A (about ₹1,000 crores invested, now ₹3,000-3,500 crores value, NSE and CIBIL assets) to return money over 6-18 months; launches to be planned around that redemption.

qa_highlights.question: How does the ROE path to 20-25% look?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about 20% tangible ROE over 3-3.5 years by doubling profits; 18-20% blended ROE considered comfortable given NBFC lending and 3-4% sponsor capital on alternates.

risks_watch: Mark-to-market volatility on treasury and NSE-linked fair value; other income was negative ₹44 crores this quarter.
Carry lumpiness and reversals; ~₹60 crores of carry this quarter; future carry sensitive to exits from funds.
AMC outflows from P1A redemption of ₹3,000-3,500 crores over 6-18 months; institutional mandate flow recovery to be confirmed.
UBS flow conversion versus the $600-700 million target and the warrant conversion timing (~February).
Competitive intensity from PE-backed digital players in UHNI, HNI and affluent segments; management says margins should hold.
Cost-to-income path toward 46-47% while adding senior hires; possible temporary rise of 100-200 bps during builds.
summary.management_tone: Confident on wealth flows, platform breadth and UBS progress, but cautious on near-term AMC flows and TBR, which management called soft and structurally changing. Management was specific about targets and open about the carry and mark-to-market effects.
key_quotes: The UHNI franchise remains the firm's anchor with unchanged priorities, grow share of wallet, widen our reach beyond the metros, and be the first call for families after a liquidity event.
We do not judge COMPASS on usage, but on definite outcomes, which is efficiency, commercial impact, quality, and control.
If we can double our profits over the next 3.5 years and, honestly, don't see any need to raise capital. We can ensure that we hit the 20% number.

adds.what: Full-stack capital markets platform (not productive capacity; readiness by end-March/early April 2027)

growth.why: Guidance is for UBS cross-flows of $600-700M in FY27 (about $300-325M in last three months), cost-to-operating income improvement of 100-150 bps, and ROE target ~20% over 3-3.5 years, backed by concrete flow run-rate and cost trends but few hard capacity numbers; reported revenue +4.8% YoY (after a negative other income) while ARR revenue grew 27.5%.
